Heron's Formula

GeometryAreaTriangles
Game: Drag the corners of a triangle and watch how the circle inside it can measure the space it covers; there is nothing to win.
How to play: Drag A, B or C with a mouse or finger, or focus a corner and use the arrow keys. Press Show names for the labels and Check the formula to see the two areas agree.
Look for the math

Moving one corner changes the size and shape of the triangle, yet two very different ways of working out its space inside always give the same answer. The applet shows why: a circle tucked into the corners cuts the triangle into pieces that can be laid out as a rectangle.

Heron's formula

Write the side lengths as a, b, c and half the perimeter as s = (a + b + c)/2. Heron's formula says the area is

S² = s(s - a)(s - b)(s - c)

The circle touches each side at a point. The two pieces of a side meeting at a corner have equal lengths from that corner: call them x = s - a, y = s - b, z = s - c. Then s = x + y + z and the formula becomes S² = sxyz. The logic test checked this at thousands of triangles, including flat and very thin ones, comparing it with the area measured straight from the three corner positions.

Six pieces make a rectangle

The incircle meets the sides at right angles, so each of the six small triangles has height r, the inradius. At the bottom of the picture they are laid side by side into a rectangle r high and x + y + z = s wide. Its area is rs, but it is also the whole triangle, so S = rs. Turn on Show names to see the three widths.

The product identity

Let I be the centre of the circle and w = AI. Splitting the angles at the corners in half gives cot α = x/r, cot β = y/r, cot γ = z/r with α + β + γ = 90°. The right-hand diagram shows the identity

xyz = r²(x + y + z) = r²s

which is the same as the trigonometric rule cot α + cot β + cot γ = cot α cot β cot γ. Together with S = rs it gives sxyz = r²s² = S², finishing the proof. The logic test checked both identities and the angle rule for every triangle it tried.

From a four-sided shape to a triangle

The page also notes that Heron's formula is a special case of Brahmagupta's formula for a four-sided shape drawn inside a circle: let one side shrink to nothing and the two corners at its ends merge into one. The logic test checked that Brahmagupta's area really approaches Heron's as the fourth side tends to zero. The applet keeps the touch-point construction and the "Show names" checkbox; its old green panel and checkbox have been replaced by this page's controls.

Try making a long, thin triangle, then press Check the formula. The strip at the bottom gets very narrow, but its area still matches the number from Heron's formula.
